note: Merged from eight batch files, each scored by its own independent agent.

scores.notes: Icon-style Jesus standing in the boat, arm outstretched, with about twelve disciples clinging and bailing; matches the scene. A flat gilded border strip about 25px wide runs across the top edge and down the upper left and right edges around the inset dark cloud panel, reading as a painted gold frame.

Night sea: Peter at the gunwale (centre-left) with one bare foot on the rim and the other stepping onto the water, disciples gripping the boat at left, Jesus standing on the waves at right-centre, torn sail top-left, shore lamps right. Painting reaches all four edges; no lettering in any corner.

Ink-and-watercolor: Jesus centred before a dark, empty rock-cut tomb pointing in with mouth open, Martha in red shawl with clasped hands at front left, crowd framing both sides and Bethany houses at upper right. Washes reach all four borders; no lettering found in corners or on rocks.

Villagers under the olive tree at left: an elder with a staff points toward the walled city, a woman carries a jar on her shoulder, and two children and a man listen. A donkey is tied to the stone wall and a Roman soldier stands at the right edge. The painting reaches all four borders, and I found no lettering in the corners or on the buildings.

Golden shafts of light fall from the upper left onto dark swirling waters; the bright area holds only brushwork with no face or figure for God. Painting reaches all four borders and no lettering is in any corner.

Ink-and-watercolor: Peter mid-leap clutching his coat toward the water, beloved disciple standing in the boat pointing to the shore, others hauling a fish-heavy net at right; no lettering. The upper-left sky and left-edge water soften toward white paper (style-allowed fade, no frame); minor oddity that the splash rings already form beneath the still-airborne Peter.

Moses with staff and raised arm beside Aaron, pig rooting mid-right, Israelites ringed, glory cloud with rays over the tabernacle (no form); watercolor fades to white paper at the corners and bottom edge. A clear numeral-like '3' glyph is painted on the white gate panel of the tabernacle courtyard (center, just left of middle).

Ink-and-watercolor interior painted to all four borders: the Levite kneels at right of center with the knife held over the still, covered body on a mat, the act only implied; lamp on a low stand, donkey in the doorway at left, cloaks and jars at right. No lettering in corners or on objects.

Wide gilded vertical frame bands run down the full left and right edges. Greek-style letters (O, Ω, N shapes) sit inside the cross halo at top center, and a small signature-like scribble is in the water at bottom right just inside the gold band.

Icon-style child leads wolf/lamb, leopard, goat, calf and lion with a shepherd at right, matching the scene, but the child's cruciform halo (centre) carries Greek letters O, Ω, N, which is visible lettering and marks the unnamed child as Christ. Edges are fully painted.

Icon-style gold ground: Abraham raises a knife over bound Isaac on wood atop a stone altar, bundled firewood in front, tent and well lower right. Only plain light rays at top centre with no figure; gold and landscape reach every edge with no inscriptions.

Fire and sulfur streak down from a bright break in the clouds (top center) onto a walled mud-brick city at left, with palms, pits and fleeing robed figures shielding their faces. The light contains no figure. Only one city mass is clearly shown. In this ink-and-watercolor style, small patches of bare paper show at the left edge sky and the bottom-left corner.

Jesus stands center-right at the mast with both arms outstretched over a night sea with moon breaking through clouds; five disciples frame the lower edge, one in the center holding a bucket. Full bleed on all edges, no lettering; the waves are still breaking rather than calming, which fits the moment of the rebuke.

Dark oil-style seascape with a swirling column of light entering from the top center and spreading over the waves; zoomed light shows only brushstroke cloud, no face or figure for God. Paint reaches all four borders (dark vignette only), no lettering.

Bald Elisha in fur mantle walks the rocky road in the left foreground while a band of tunic-clad youths pours out of Bethel's stone gate with raised arms, shouting, in dust; oil painting fills all four borders and corners are clean.

Oil-style painting reaching all borders: Jericho's wall crumbles in dust at left, priests in white and violet blow ram's horns at lower left beside a gold chest, and Joshua with spear and sword leads the shouting crowd at center right. Sun rays in the sky contain no figure; no lettering anywhere.

The Levite kneels beside the still woman on a mat, knife held in his hand, with the act only implied; the lamp is at bottom center and the tethered donkey is in the doorway at upper left. The painting runs to all four edges, and no lettering appears in any corner.

Jesus centre in a braced lunge with right arm raised toward the dark, empty tomb mouth; Martha in red with clasped hands at left-centre and mourners flanking both sides; Bethany houses on the gold sky. Stance is turned toward the viewer with mouth closed, but it reads as the call; edges full, no lettering.

Job in torn tunic and purple cloak stands barefoot on an ash heap with potsherds, a dust whirlwind sweeping in from the right; the bright core of the storm (upper right) is lightning and white light only, with no face or figure. Dark night sky at left over a walled city; painted to all edges, no lettering.

There is only one seraph (top center). Its face is uncovered under a hood of wings, its bare feet are visible, and it holds tongs with a burning coal, which is the moment of Isaiah 6:6, not the veiled seraphim of 6:2. Isaiah (lower left) and the gilded temple with smoke are right. No figure of God appears, and the cherub carvings on the walls are décor.

Nine bowed Israelites sit by a reed-lined canal at dusk with two harps on the grass and a ziggurat and walls on the far bank. The ink-and-watercolor fades to white paper at the bottom corners and left/right edges (style-acceptable margin); the ink hatching on the bottom-right rock is grass/texture, not lettering.

Icon-style Saul center with arm raised in a ring of light, companions shielding eyes, donkey with baggage and Damascus walls at right; gold ground and halo have no lettering and paint reaches all edges. The kneeling companion beside the donkey (lower right) has three arms: one holding the bridle plus two hands reaching to the ground.

Lion, calf, man and eagle creatures with eyes on wings and robes stand on a glassy sea with mist, rainbow arch and a radiant starburst above a central gold ark-like chest; the light contains no face or figure, and no lettering on the chest relief or jeweled wall panels. Lion and eagle are robed with crossed arms, and the throne is rendered as a gold chest, but nothing contradictory.

The stone is still loaded in David's sling pouch (left) while a second stone sits on an antenna-like stalk on Goliath's helmet, and Goliath topples backward rather than onto his face. Top is unpainted white paper and the bottom edge fades to paper (watercolor style).

A gilded frame band runs along the top, left and right edges. Moses (left of center) holds a staff in each hand, so two staffs, instead of an open hand stretched over the sea, and a large crowd already stands far out on the seabed while the sea is still parting; the pillar at top center is only a column of fire and light with no figure.

Icon-style Jericho wall collapsing in dust (centre-left) with linen-robed priests blowing ram's horns (centre-right) and Joshua with spear leading a shouting crowd (lower right). The crowd faces and walks toward the viewer rather than surging into the breach, and a few small figures stand atop the falling stones; edges full, no lettering.

Empty luminous landscape with no figures; the lower half is a flat mirror-like expanse with faint panel seams, but with grassy shores at left and right and cloud reflections it reads at normal size as a calm lake or sea, which cuts against 'the sea is no more'. Faint city towers on both horizons; painted to all edges, no lettering.

David (center right, blue robe, with a lyre and sheathed blade beside him) reclines on the grass by a still pool. Sheep lie and graze, and there is a stone fold, village roofs, a staff against the rocks and a jar at the pool edge. The watercolor reaches all borders, and the bottom-right corner shows only grass strokes, no initials.

Three kneeling Roman soldiers spread red, blue and brown garments and drop small bone lots in the foreground; Jesus hangs on the center cross with head inclined and a blank title board, two empty crosses flank him, distant onlookers left and right. Watercolor fades to white paper on all four edges (style-acceptable); one long-haired bearded onlooker right of the right cross loosely resembles Jesus but reads as a bystander.

Fiery streaks rain from a radiant cloud opening at top center onto two walled mud-brick cities, palms and burning fields, with small unnamed onlookers shielding their faces on the rise below; the radiance is clouds and light only, no figure for Yahweh. Paint reaches all edges; no lettering in corners.

Jesus stands centre before a rock-cut tomb with the round stone rolled aside, head lifted and right arm raised high (upward rather than into the tomb), crowd of mourners left and kneeling right, Martha front-left with clasped hands; tomb mouth dark and empty. Oil painting fills all borders, no lettering in corners.

Jonah sits hunched inside a ribbed, seaweed-hung fish interior with dark painted corners and no figure for Yahweh, but the bottom-right corner carries a painted signature-like inscription ("Ton… 1020…") with a smaller scribble just left of it.

The central elder with a staff wears a gold halo amid a group of men, so he reads as Jesus or a saint with disciples rather than an ordinary villager, and the 'synagogue' is a Byzantine church with cross-topped domes. A signature-like scribble is painted on the road below the Roman soldier's feet at bottom right.

Saul staggers on the Damascus road shielding his eyes beneath a shaft of white light from the sky (top centre, no figure or face in the beam); two companions recoil and one kneels, a man holds a laden donkey at right, walled Damascus on the horizon. Edges full, no lettering.

Icon-style: bald bearded Elisha with staff on the road (centre bottom) and a band of youths pouring from the gate pointing at him, golden calf on a plinth in the city. But Bethel is drawn as a Byzantine walled city whose domes carry three Christian crosses (top centre-left), an anachronism in a 9th-century BC Israelite town; edges painted, no lettering.

The sea is not divided: the right half shows a single towering storm wave and surf breaking on the shore, with no second wall of water and no dry sea floor. Moses with his staff and the Israelites stand along the beach at left. A fiery cloud column (top center) contains no figure.

The whole picture sits inside a painted gold-leaf frame on all four sides, with a flat gold sky. Moses (left) raises his hand skyward rather than toward the pig, Aaron in breastpiece beside him, pig rooting center-right with a ring of Israelites; only a small white cloud over the tabernacle, no figure; breastpiece stones carry no lettering.

Watercolor: Naomi seated center holding the infant, Ruth in a rust-red cloak and Boaz with staff beside her, three women in the lamplit doorway at left, basket set aside; anatomy and hands read correctly, no lettering. Bottom-left and bottom-right corners break into white paper (style-allowed soft fade).

Paul off-centre left in a stone lane with closed scroll under his arm, terraced hillside, distant city, a few travelers down the lane and stormy clouds with golden break; the window oil lamp (upper left) is lit with a flame rather than unlit. Watercolor fades to white paper along the left edge, otherwise no text.

Icon-style plain with both walled cities burning under fireballs streaming from a radiant cloud burst at top center that holds no face or figure; however, a small cursive inscription (reads like "Shkes") is painted on the ground beside the crack at lower center, next to the veiled woman.

Ink-and-watercolor child leading a wolf with a lamb, a lying leopard by a goat, a calf and a young lion along a Judean vineyard path, with a shepherd in the distance at right (oddly holding two staffs). The only edge issue is a soft fade to white paper at bottom left, which is part of the style.

Ink-and-watercolor: Jesus stands by the mast (centre) with arm outstretched over a calming sea under breaking storm clouds, disciples crouched at the gunwales and one bailing with a scoop (centre-right). Wash is painted to all four borders; no lettering in corners.

Wet, bearded Jonah sits hunched against slick ribbed flesh with a dark throat-tunnel behind him, but a gaping jaw of large teeth fills the left third, so he reads as sitting in the fish's open mouth rather than the enclosed belly the scene asks for (no opening). No figure for God; dark paint reaches all edges, no lettering.

Moses (left center) holds his staff and stretches his hand toward a sea parted into two curling walls with a dry rocky channel between. Israelites line the shore and a pillar of fire and cloud rises at top center with no figure in it. An unrequested walled town sits on the far shore. In this ink-and-watercolor style, a ragged white paper edge runs down the right border and parts of the bottom.

The Shulammite stands left of center, mouth open, gesturing toward wild roses and lilies, with blossoming trees, a stone village and a freestanding shepherd's staff at right. Soft watercolor fade to pale paper along the left edge and bottom corners (style-acceptable); a faint dark wash stroke in the foliage near the bottom right (about x 1075) is not legible as initials.

Watercolor: an elder with staff pointing toward a distant walled city, woman with water jar, family group under an olive tree, tethered donkey at left and a Roman soldier far right on the road; tower windows are dots, not lettering. Top-right sky and bottom-left corner fade to white paper (style-allowed).

Saul mid-stride centre with arm raised under a swirling burst of light (no form in it), two companions shielding eyes at left, a third with a laden donkey at right, Damascus walls on the horizon; the city includes an anachronistic dome and minaret (right background). Small white-paper patches show at the left and top-right borders in the watercolor.

Oil-style painting reaching all borders: the veiled Shulammite stands right of center with hand extended toward wild roses and lilies, blossoming trees at right and a hill village at left. The shepherd's staff at right stands upright on its own in the grass (minor); no lettering in any corner.

Ink-and-watercolor fall of Jericho's wall in dust, with priests in blue blowing ram's horns on both sides and Joshua with a spear at right foreground. The shouting crowd faces and runs toward the viewer, away from the breach rather than into the city, and the paint fades softly to paper at bottom right.

Three soldiers kneel casting dice over Jesus's garments below three crosses, matching the scene, but a plain gold icon border runs down the full left and right edges outside the landscape, and Jesus's cruciform halo (top centre) carries small glyph-like marks in its arms.

Icon-style gold sky with blue clouds and plain light rays (no figure) over a pale, smooth, textured basin ringed by hills where the sea was; the basin is opaque and dry-looking rather than water. Paint and gold reach every edge; no inscriptions in the gold.

There is only one seraph (top center right). Its lower face and its bare feet are uncovered, and it holds tongs with a glowing coal, which is the moment of Isaiah 6:6, not the veiled seraphim of 6:2. Isaiah stoops at lower left in the temple hall with smoke. The glowing inner doorway and dais (center right) are empty, with no figure of God. A tiny round medallion on the doorframe is ornament, not writing.

Abraham stands center with the knife raised overhead and his other hand on Isaac's chest; Isaac lies on wood over a stone altar, with the sunrise, tent and well at right and a firewood bundle and staff at lower left. Isaac is not bound (hands and feet free; the ropes only tie the wood), and the watercolor fades to pale paper at the top-left and bottom-left corners (style-acceptable).

Icon-style Peter stepping from the boat onto the waves toward a haloed Jesus, disciples in the boat at left; Jesus's cross-nimbus (top center-right) has glyph-like letter marks in its arms. Gold daylight ground replaces the requested night sky.

Bare-chested Peter clutching his coat is airborne between the boats (centre-left) while a large impact splash already erupts on the water below and ahead of him, before he has entered it; beloved disciple points from the middle boat and others haul a full net in the foreground boat. Edges painted full, no lettering; the splash-before-entry may read as motion shorthand, hence uncertain.

Four winged living creatures (lion, man, calf, eagle) with eyes covering their wings flank an empty marble throne under a rainbow, with a misty glass floor in front; the throne holds no figure. Ink-and-watercolor edges soft-fade to white paper at the corners (style margin, not a frame); the eyes are eyes, and there is no lettering.

Naomi sits on a bench holding the swaddled infant, beside Ruth in a rust-red cloak, Boaz with a staff, a gleaning basket, a lit lamp in the glowing doorway and three Bethlehem women at right. The painting fills all four edges, and no lettering appears.

The Ancient of Days appears only as a white-cored flame above burning wheels (top centre), with no face or figure in it, and Daniel looks up at lower left. But five haloed, winged angels stand or sit beside the empty thrones in the clouds (top left and top right), a host the scene leaves out, and the sky behind is gold rather than night.

A white-robed seated figure with head, hands resting on the armrests and feet is drawn on the flaming wheeled throne (top centre), giving the Ancient of Days a human form. Daniel on a Babylon rooftop and the ziggurat skyline are fine; a tiny decorative frieze on a lower-left building is indistinct, not legible lettering; edges painted throughout.

The center of the frame is a large reflective body of water with shorelines and ripple lines that reads as a sea or lake, which contradicts 'the sea is no more' and the request for no visible water. The hills, dawn clouds and light shafts are fine, and no figures appear. In this ink-and-watercolor style, the left and right edges and the bottom corners fade to white paper.

Job, with sores and a torn ash-stained tunic, stands center on the ash heap of shards, while a dust whirlwind with lightning sweeps in at left; the vortex contains no face or figure. The right half of the sky is flat icon gold rather than storm, but there is no halo, lettering or frame, and the painting reaches all four edges.

Oil-style Abraham center with knife raised over Isaac, who lies bound on wood atop a stone altar on a rocky ridge, with a tent and well far right; bright clouds above hold no figure. Paint reaches all edges, no lettering.

Icon-style Ezekiel stands left of centre in a valley strewn with skulls and bones under a gold sky (no figure in the sky; God absent); instead of lifting an arm and speaking he is writing with a stylus on a blank tablet, the other hand open low toward the bones. Painting reaches all borders, tablet is blank.

Icon-style round brick pit with Daniel standing among five lions with closed mouths, a figureless light beam above, and two guards at the back gate. Darius leans on the rim at upper left (standing, not kneeling, drawn at hierarchical scale), and there is no lid or palace courtyard; the small brown marks at the left edge are pebble strokes like those elsewhere, not lettering.

Moses with a staff and Aaron in a high-priest ephod stand at left, a pig roots in the center, Israelites cluster at right, and the tabernacle is behind. God's presence is only a small glowing cloud with light rays above the tabernacle at top center, with no figure; Moses gestures toward Aaron rather than at the pig.

A child (centre) leads a lion on a cord, with wolf and lamb, a leopard lying beside a goat, and two calves along a path in sunlit terraced Judean hills; a shepherd watches at left and a walled city gate sits at right. Edges full, no lettering.

Moses with staff (foreground left) extends his arm across Aaron in priestly breastplate toward a pig rooting in the scrub, with Israelites in a loose ring, tents and the tabernacle under a plain pinkish cloud (no figure) behind. Breastplate stones are blank; painted to all edges, no signature.

An old man lies dead on a woven mat (foreground) with his eyes closed and hands on his chest, and cords bind his ankles. Five mourners sit with bowed heads, with tents, mud-brick houses, a staff against a tent and a grazing flock (right) behind. In this ink-and-watercolor style, the top-right sky and the bottom corners fade softly to paper, and I found no lettering.

A pale painted scribble like a signature ('ꞩbiel') sits on the bottom edge at center-right, below the right-hand rock (about x 1030-1080). The single seraph at top is a knotted tangle of wings with two faces partly exposed, and it holds tongs with a burning coal (the later 6:6 moment) instead of seraphim veiling face and feet; there is no figure for God in the radiance.

Icon-style Moses with staff at left before the Israelites, the sea parted into two wave walls around a cracked dry path, and a faint smoke-and-fire pillar with no figure; a gilded painted frame surrounds the whole picture on all four sides.

Grieving exiles sit and weep on a reedy bank in the foreground with three lyres lying unplayed in the grass, river across the middle, Babylon walls and ziggurat at right under a dusk sky with sunset and first stars. Painting fills all borders (only a tiny dark compression block in the top-right corner), no lettering.

Oil-style painting reaching all borders: the father, cloak flying, embraces and kisses his ragged son on a dusty road at center, with a Galilee lakeside village behind. Three small household figures (two at the courtyard gate, one at a window, right) stand where one servant was asked, which is minor; no lettering.

Four winged creatures covered in eyes (lion, ox, man-faced, eagle) stand in two pairs either side of a sea of glass. The jeweled throne at center under a rainbow arch is empty, with no figure, face or hands, so God appears only as glow. A small gold chest in front of the throne is an unrequested extra, and the bottom band is the glass slab's crystalline edge, not a frame.

The father in a red robe embraces his ragged son on a winding road, with a servant at the white house door at right. But at the son's left shoulder (centre) one hand grips the shoulder while a second open hand juts out beside it, giving the pair an extra hand, and a small scribbled signature-like mark sits on the ground near the bottom edge, right of centre (about x1040–1090).

Icon-style: Peter, coat clutched to his chest, plunges from the boat in a burst of spray toward a small haloed Christ on the far shore (upper left); a disciple stands in the boat pointing shoreward while six others haul a net full of fish. Jesus on the shore is supported by the verse though not in the plan; the boat's pointing disciple looks Christ-like but has no halo. The halo holds only a cross with no letters; gold and water reach every edge.

David (center foreground) holds his sling with the stone still in its pouch while Goliath (center right) already lies face down in the dust, so the stone has both been thrown and not thrown. The Israelites at left and the crested Philistine ranks at right fit the scene. The painting reaches all borders, and I found no lettering.

Small isolated ink glyphs, an 'F' and a 'c', sit on the ribbed wall near the top-right corner (about x 1290-1310, y 15-45). Otherwise Jonah sits hunched against the left wall of a ribbed, seaweed-hung fish gullet with no figure for God; a faint glow far down the tunnel and pale paper at the bottom corners (style-acceptable) are minor.

Icon-style Jonah sits hunched and soaked inside the ribbed red-gold belly with seaweed, no figure for God; but the curved ribs on the left (center-left, around Jonah's shoulder height) carry columns of faint glyph-like pseudo-script. Paint reaches all edges.

Dark, wind-lined deep waters with a burst of white-gold light streaming down from the top-centre edge; the light is unpainted paper and rays with no face, head or silhouette in it. Watercolor washes reach all four borders; no lettering.

Ink-and-watercolor courtyard den: Daniel stands at center looking up among five calm lions with closed mouths, Darius kneels at the rim at upper right, and four guards stand at upper left; the warm glow above Daniel holds no figure. Pale washes reach all borders; the scroll case at his hip is plain and there is no lettering (no lid visible, which is minor).

Peter leaps from the boat's edge into splashing water clutching his coat, the beloved disciple stands pointing toward the shore at left, and four disciples haul a fish-filled net at right. Gold-leaf sky and painted sea run to all four edges, with no lettering in the corners.

Icon-style David reclines on green grass beside a still pool with sheep lying down, staff, lyre, water jar, sheepfold and village; the LORD is not shown in any form. A faint, tone-on-tone mark like two small glyphs sits on the rock face at top right (about x1180, y115); it may be rock texture, but at zoom it reads like an inscription.

Daniel seen from behind and beside looks up at a night cloud court: an empty white-glowing throne wrapped in fire with two burning wheels, and four empty stone thrones placed around it; no face, head or robe in the light even when brightened. Babylon's walls and ziggurats below; painted to all edges, no lettering.

Goliath (center) topples backward through the air with the stone at his brow while two swords and a spear fly loose around him. Under his feet lies a second red-crested armored body face down in the dust, which reads as a duplicate fallen Goliath or an unexplained corpse, and the text says he fell on his face. The gold-leaf icon style reaches all borders with no frame or lettering.

The father, robe flying and one foot kicked up in a run, embraces the ragged son center-frame on a dusty road, with a whitewashed house and arched gate at left where a woman servant pauses, and the lake with boats at right. Watercolor fades to paper at the top-left and bottom-right corners (style-acceptable); the hand flung out at left reads as the son's far arm, so there is no clear extra limb, and there is no lettering.

Icon-influenced Paul left of center with blank scrolls tucked at his side, stone lane and walls, small distant travelers, terraced hills and a far city under swirling clouds; scrolls and stones show no lettering. The window lamp at right is lit rather than unlit, a minor deviation.

Ezekiel stands right of centre with his right arm lifted toward the skulls and bones that fill the valley, low hills behind, nothing representing God in the sky. The ink-and-watercolor washes fade to cream paper at the top corners, left edge and bottom corners (style margin); the wooden case at his belt shows only grain.

Icon panel with a raised gold painted frame on all four sides, and Jesus's cross-nimbus (center) carries the letters Ο / Ω / Ν. Otherwise the scene fits: Jesus raises his arm toward the empty dark tomb at right, and haloed Martha with clasped hands stands before the crowd at left.

Job, ragged and bare-headed with a staff, stands on a grey ash heap littered with broken pottery while a dust whirlwind with a lightning-lit bright core bears in from the left. Zoomed, the bright core and funnel contain only light, cloud and debris, with no face or figure; walled city at right, and edges full.

Daniel stands calmly in the stone pit among resting lions with closed mouths, King Darius kneels on the rim at upper right, the wooden lid is pushed back at upper left, and distant guards stand in the courtyard. The angel/God is suggested only by pale light rays at top centre, with no figure in them; edges full, no lettering.

David reclines on green grass in the mid-ground beside a still pool with a clay water jar, staff leaning against him, with sheep lying all around, a stone sheepfold at left and village roofs on the hill at right in warm late light. Painted to all edges; no lettering or signature in the corners.

The Shulammite (center) stands in a field of red roses and white lilies, gesturing toward the flowers, with blossoming trees, a staff against a rock and a village (right) under a gold-leaf sky. She wears a plain gold-outlined halo with nothing inside it, which may make her read as the Virgin Mary. A small dark sprig on the rock (lower left of center) is not lettering, and the edges are fully painted.

Peter sits on the gunwale at right center with one bare foot touching the water, and the disciples crowd the boat under a torn patched sail; Jesus stands mid-distance on the water at left. Jesus' feet sink to the ankles, so he looks partly as if he is wading, and Peter is seated rather than stepping out; the watercolor fades to paper at the left and bottom edges (style-acceptable), and there is no lettering.

Watercolor: bald Elisha in a fur mantle walks the dusty road in the foreground while a band of youths pours from the city gate jeering with raised arms; no lettering. Sky wash stops short of the top corners and the bottom-right fades to paper (style-allowed); Elisha is larger in frame than requested.

The interior wall stops at the right third and becomes a bright gold-sky daytime landscape with a walled city, while the doorway at left shows night; it is half room, half outdoor scene. The concubine lies with eyes open and gaze alert under the raised knife (centre-left), so she reads as alive, not a still body, and the Levite holds a staff as well as the knife.

Oil-style painting reaching all borders: Naomi sits at the doorway with the infant at center, Boaz in blue behind her, Ruth in a rust-red cloak at right of center, three women of Bethlehem at right and one seated at lower left, and a lamp lit inside the door. Hands around the child read plausibly; no lettering in corners or on objects.

An elderly white-bearded man lies on a woven mat with hands folded at his chest, while three pairs of mourners sit close in grief before tents and mud-brick huts with a grazing flock at right. Zoomed, his eyes are open and gazing upward rather than closed, so he reads as dying rather than dead; edges are full and no lettering appears.

Nine exiles sit huddled on the grassy riverbank (lower half), heads bowed, faces in their hands, with two lyres and a bundle lying unplayed in front; the canal crosses the middle and walled Babylon with ziggurats lies on the far bank under an amber-to-gold sky. Edges full, no lettering.

The scene sits inside a wide raised gold icon-panel border with a bevelled inner frame on all four sides. Soldiers kneel around a cloth with dice-like lots at the cross's foot, yet the crucified Jesus (top centre) still wears a dark blue cloak draped over his shoulder, contradicting the dividing of his clothing; the titulus and halo are blank.

An old man with a halo, in a skin garment, lies dead on a woven mat (center) with three women mourning. Tents with a staff against a post, mud-brick houses and grazing sheep sit under a gold sky. The center mourner wears a red mantle over a blue cap with a small cluster of dots like the Virgin Mary's star on her brow (center, above the halo), so icon-literate readers may see Mary at Adam's death. The cue is small, so I can't say whether it counts as a blocker. I found no inscriptions on the gold, and the edges are fully painted.

Ezekiel stands right of center in a coarse mantle with his right arm raised toward the bone-strewn valley; a blank wooden tablet is in his left hand, and skulls and bones cover the floor up to the hills under a low warm sun. The bright sky at left holds only clouds with no figure for God, the painting reaches all four edges, and the tablet face shows no lettering.

Oil-style Paul left of center with a blank scroll under his arm and a scroll case at his belt, stone lane and house at left, terraced hillside and distant city under heavy clouds with low light, a few distant travelers; no lettering, paint to all edges. The window lamp is lit rather than unlit (minor).

Four kneeling Roman soldiers sort garments and cast dice-like lots in the foreground, but Jesus on the centre-right cross is still fully dressed in a white tunic and blue mantle, contradicting the division of his clothing below. Titulus board is blank, the two side crosses are empty, and the oil painting fills all borders.
